subject: Clarify SKU split, support escalation paths, and platform fee amortization
messages:
From: Alicia Burns <aburns@acmerobotics.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwoodai.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: SKU split / support tiers / platform fee questions

Hi Priya —

Thanks again for the demo this week. We're working to line up internal stakeholders for a private VPC deployment and I have a few items we need clarified before we lock the next procurement meeting: 

- Can you share a clear SKU split for an on‑prem deployment (license per GPU vs. per‑node vs. concurrent token throughput)?
- How should we think about the platform fee across the first 2 years? Is there a way to amortize it against committed spend?
- Support tiers: what's included in Premium vs Enterprise (response times, number of named engineers, runbook updates, on‑site options)?
- Escalation path for Sev1 incidents — specific SLA credits and escalation contact model (weekends / holidays)?
- Any migration credits or pilot discounts for a two‑region rollout (US + EU)?

We are targeting a Q3 pilot with ~8 nodes (NVIDIA H100 equivalent), expected peak concurrent sessions ~200, sustained per‑token throughput profile attached (Acme-MAP-v1.xlsx).

If you can send a short one‑page summary we can circulate to procurement this week, that would be ideal.

Thanks,
Alicia
Alicia Burns
Head of ML Infrastructure
Acme Robotics

Attachments: Acme-MAP-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwoodai.com>
To: Alicia Burns <aburns@acmerobotics.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SKU split / support tiers / platform fee questions

Alicia —

Appreciate the details and the MAP file. Quick answers inline, then I'll follow up with a consolidated one‑page summary and a draft SOW.

• SKU split: We offer three SKU models for private deployments — license per GPU (recommended for bursty workloads), license per node (predictable flat cost), and a throughput SKU (tokens/sec) for extremely variable clusters. For an 8‑node H100 footprint you typically land in our node + platform fee model; I can produce a table with estimated list prices and per‑token unit economics once I confirm your expected average seq length and retention window.

• Platform fee amortization: We can offer a first‑year credit against the platform fee tied to committed spend. Typical approach: 25–40% credit on platform fee for a 12–36 month committed contract depending on commit size.

• Support tiers: Standard (business hours, email), Premium (24/7 pager, 4‑hour Sev1, named TAM, quarterly runbook reviews), Enterprise (24/7 + on‑site quarterly, SLA-backed response, dedicated engineering hours). I will attach our standard SLO table and a suggested Enterprise escalation path.

• Sev1 escalation: Weekend escalation to on‑call with 1‑hour initial response, staffed rotation for Enterprise. SLA credits scale with incident duration; we can put firm numbers in the SOW.

• Migration credits / pilot discounts: We can give a one‑time migration credit (dollar amount) or a first‑year platform fee waiver — open to whichever maps better to Acme's procurement model.

Next steps: I'll pull pricing options and a draft SOW & proposal for your team. If you can confirm average seq length and retention window, I'll lock the numbers.

Sharing SOW template for procurement to review.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
priya_natarajan@redwoodai.com

Attachments: SOW-template.pdf (pdf)

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwoodai.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodai.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodai.com>, Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwoodai.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 13:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: SKU split / support tiers / platform fee questions — need pricing guidance

Team — forwarding Acme's questions (see original below). Pilot size: 8 H100 nodes, peak concurrent sessions ~200, want two‑region (US+EU) plan. Procurement wants something they can take to legal this week. Proposed concessions I'm thinking of: 

- Offer node‑based SKU for baseline; provide per‑GPU overlay for burst.
- Platform fee credit: propose 30% first year if they commit to 24 months and a $750k ARR equivalent.
- Migration credit: $50k one‑time credit for migration professional services.
- Discounting: sliding scale — 10% for 12m commit, 15% for 24m, 20% for 36m on licenses; allow a stacking rule with platform credits capped at 30%.
- Support: map Premium -> 4h Sev1, Enterprise -> 1h Sev1 + named eng + on‑site quarterly.

Questions: 
1) Are these concessions feasible from an S&M + finance exposure POV?
2) Any constraints from Delivery on on‑site quarterly visits for EU?
3) Alex — are there SW install SOW gotchas for multi‑region that would require higher migration credits?

Would like quick thumbs — procurement wants a one‑page summary Monday.

Thanks — Priya

> Hi Priya —
> 
> Thanks again for the demo this week...

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodai.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwoodai.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodai.com>, Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwoodai.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 16:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: SKU split / support tiers / platform fee questions — pricing guidance

Priya / team —

Quick recommendations that balance competitiveness and exposure: 

1) Discounts: Approve sliding scale but tighten the caps — 8% (12m), 14% (24m), 20% (36m) on licenses. Keep a hard cap of 30% total effective concession (discount + credits). Finance ok with that.

2) Platform fee credit: Approve up to 30% first year for 24m+ commitments; do not waive platform fee entirely unless we have >$1.5M committed ARR.

3) Migration credit: $50k baseline for standard migration; for cross‑region (EU on‑site or compliance work) allow up to $85k if SOW shows additional travel/compliance costs.

4) Support / SLA: Approve Premium (4h Sev1 response) and Enterprise (1h Sev1 + named eng + periodic on‑site). For Enterprise, include a clause for priority routing and two named escalation contacts.

5) Escalation: Weekend pager for Enterprise, second‑level (engineering) contact with 2‑hour follow up, and monthly RCA cadence until closure for Sev1s. SLA credits: incremental credits at 4h, 12h, 24h thresholds.

6) Legal: Require a standard indemnity/limitations carve‑out for hardware failures in on‑prem deployments.

Alex — note the migration uplift if customer requires full EU on‑site install & data residency work.

I'll attach a quick price adjustment workbook.

Vivek

Attachments: pricing_mod_2026.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwoodai.com>
To: Alicia Burns <aburns@acmerobotics.com>, Jamal Ortega <jamal.ortega@acmerobotics.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodai.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodai.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 14:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Redwood proposal: SKU & support summary for Acme two‑region pilot (draft)

Alicia / Jamal —

Thanks for the patience. Attached is a concise draft proposal and pricing summary for the two‑region pilot + private VPC deployment. Key points below (one‑page summary attached as proposal_v1.pdf):

- Recommended SKU: Node‑based SKU for baseline (8 nodes), with optional per‑GPU burst overlay. Estimated list license: $X/month per node (detailed in attached table).
- Platform fee: 30% credit applied to platform fee in year 1 assuming a 24‑month commitment (we can revise with longer commit).
- Migration credit: $50,000 one‑time credit; up to $85,000 if EU on‑site/certification work required (SOW dependent).
- Discounts: tiered discounting — 8% (12m), 14% (24m), 20% (36m) on license line items. Total concessions capped at 30% effective.
- Support tiers: 
  • Premium — 24/7 first‑response, 4h initial response for Sev1, named TAM, quarterly runbook reviews.
  • Enterprise — 24/7 + 1h initial response for Sev1, named engineering resource, priority routing, on‑site quarterly (if required). Includes monthly RCA until Sev1 closure.
- Escalation path: Enterprise customers get a weekend on‑call rotation and two named escalation contacts. SLA credits at 4h / 12h / 24h windows.

Next steps: If this maps to Acme's procurement appetite, we'll produce a formal SOW (using the attached template) and a DocuSign package. Suggested internal milestone: pilot SOW signed by end of Q3, deployment window Q4.

Please let me know if you want any of the figures in the table changed — we can lock firm numbers once you confirm expected average sequence length and retention window (affects token economics).

If helpful, we can do a 30‑minute procurement call later this week to walk the one‑page summary.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
